subject: Money
title: The Mortgage Machine
description: A fast breakdown of The Mortgage Machine for builders.

hook.text: A bank lends you $400,000 for a house. Over 30 years at 7%, you pay back $958,000. More than double.

buildup.text: Mortgages are the largest loan most people ever take. Banks earn interest for decades on a single sale.

discovery.text: Banks don't hold your mortgage anymore. They package thousands into securities and sell them to investors.

twist.text: Securitization lets banks make a loan, sell the risk, and lend again. It's a money-printing loop.

climax.text: This loop created the 2008 crisis. Banks didn't care about loan quality because they sold the risk immediately.

punchline.text: They lend. They sell. They repeat. You pay.

quiz.question: What happens to most mortgages after origination?
options: They're packaged into securities and sold
